propositions: Directory creation via os.makedirs happened outside the write lock before the first event file was written, leaving a window where interruption (host sleep, kill, timeout) could strand an empty ticket directory that fsck would report as MISSING_CREATE and FOREIGN_STORE_PATH.

New staging module creates both the directory and its first event file inside a staging path (.tmp-newticket-<pid>-<uuid4hex>) and publishes them atomically with os.rename under the existing write lock, eliminating the vulnerable window.

The staging directory naming convention (dot-prefixed) leverages existing fsck exclusion rules for dot-prefixed top-level entries, making temp paths invisible to both MISSING_CREATE and FOREIGN_STORE_PATH checks without scanner changes.

Batch write path (batch_stage_and_commit) and reconciler event write sites (inbound_translate._write_event_file, dispatch_one BRIDGE_ALERT) shared the same mkdir-then-first-file signature and were converted to use the staged publish mechanism.

Sweep mechanism (sweep_stale_staging) removes only .tmp-newticket-* staging dirs whose owner is provably dead (reusing write-lock v2 stamp: host + pid-namespace + start time), respecting the 043f boundary that writer cleanup touches only staging area, never store data.
Lock discipline and concurrency remain unchanged: rename still occurs under the existing write lock, ensuring an event is never visible before rebase guard and under_lock_check have passed.
